solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recording effect of Easter's start falling late, in the absence of a full moon

indicators.note: absence means the letter named next is missing from the word
the opening letter of the word drops down to the end, coming late instead of first

parts.note: the festival's name, with its possessive 's
a full moon is drawn as a round O

explanation.surface: A sound engineer muses on a recording oddity tied to Easter coming late without a full moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start falling late' moves the first E of EASTER to the end, giving ASTERE; 'in the absence of a' drops the A, leaving STERE; the full moon adds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound, played through two channels to give depth, is an effect used in sound recordings.

clue.text: Abbess, discovered shaking, becomes weak

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the remaining letters into a new order
dis-covered: the word loses its covering, its outer letters

explanation.surface: A mother superior, caught out and trembling, loses her strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the outer A and S from ABBESS to leave BBES, which 'shaking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede or decline, like a tide going out, so it means grow weaker.

clue.text: Dreadful lecher, sacked by new vice-chancellor, is emotionally unstable

indicators.note: the lecher is sacked, so his letters are taken out of the next words
new signals that the letters left over are rearranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A university head fires a dreadful lecher from the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of LECHER out of VICE-CHANCELLOR and VICCANLO remains; 'new' rearranges those. 'Dreadful' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic temper erupts without warning, so the word describes someone given to explosive, unstable feelings.

clue.text: Admission man-eater's eschewing love following indigestion on vacation?

indicators.note: following puts the ogress part after the vacated word
vacated, the word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters
eschewing means avoiding, so the letter for love is left out

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre who eats people; the 's stands for 'is'
love is zero in tennis scores, written O

explanation.surface: A man-eater, having given up love, finds herself suffering indigestion while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'indigestion' of its inside, and 'eschewing love' drops the O that stands for love (zero in tennis) from the ogress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or right of entering, so it means admission or entry.

clue.text: John's space to relax

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, a loo; with the possessive it gives LOO'S
an en is a printer's space, half the width of an em

explanation.surface: John needs a room of his own to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: John here is the toilet, not a person; an en is the printer's unit of space.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen is to slacken or ease something, which is what relaxing a grip or rule means.

clue.text: One playing Henry V?

parts.note: the actor taking the title role in Shakespeare's play is the star of the cast; Henry V himself also led his men at Agincourt

explanation.walkthrough: The actor in the title role is the star, and the king he plays literally led his army into battle, so both readings fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male role in a play or film is called this, and Henry V is such a starring part.

clue.text: Vegetation entangling a lot of grey seals?

indicators.note: entangling twists the letters together into a new order
a lot of, but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seaweed snares a group of grey seals in the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of grey' is GRE; 'entangling' mixes GRE and SEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelgrass is a seagrass growing in coastal shallows, a kind of underwater plant life.

clue.text: Uncompromising objections repelled Nobel physicist

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'
Max Born won the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics

explanation.surface: An unbending Nobel laureate in physics brushes aside every objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person refuses to yield or budge, which is to be uncompromising.

clue.text: A 6 at Lord's?

parts.note: 6 is the answer to 6 down, a leading man; at Lord's, the London cricket ground, the batsman who leads off the innings is called this

explanation.walkthrough: The 6 looks like a cricket score (a hit over the boundary) but points to 6 down, LEADING MAN. Lord's is London's famous cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the batsmen who begin an innings are its first players in, the ones who lead the side out.

clue.text: They authorise journalists to squeeze WAGs

parts.note: to press is to squeeze
wags are jokers, also called cards

explanation.surface: Reporters with accreditation squeeze footballers' wives and girlfriends for a story.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs suggests footballers' wives and girlfriends in the British tabloids, but here wags are witty people, cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Press cards are identity passes that give reporters access to events, so they act as accreditation.

clue.text: Serviceman in South Dakota sent back home temporarily

indicators.note: sent back means the combined letters are reversed
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier posted in South Dakota is sent back home for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier goes inside the state's abbreviation, and 'sent back' reverses the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for lodgings, a rented room used as a temporary residence.

clue.text: Court office constructed in Deal?

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: A law court's office building stands in the Kent town of Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal looks like the Kent seaside town, but deal is also pine or fir timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood planking, so something built from it is made of timber.

clue.text: Trademark designed to protect source of tiny stuff that's hard to find

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the anagram goes round the next letter
designed means newly put together, so the letters are rearranged
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brand is created to shield the origin of something minute and elusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges TRADEMARK, and that anagram wraps round T, the first letter of 'tiny'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark matter is the unseen mass that physicists infer but cannot detect directly.

clue.text: AN Wilson reviewed Family Guy

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looked at again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The author A N Wilson writes a review of the cartoon series Family Guy.
explanation.walkthrough: A N Wilson is a British writer and critic; Family Guy looks like the TV show title.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter's husband becomes a relative by marriage, a man in the family.

clue.text: A fault harbouring primal avidity and rapacity?

definitions.text: A fault harbouring primal avidity and rapacity?

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: primal means first, so each word gives its initial letter

explanation.surface: Greed is described as a moral failing rooted in basic hunger and grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: A and VICE take in the first letters of 'avidity' and 'rapacity'; the whole clue also describes greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth, a vice listed among the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Some elevated aristos outrival master

indicators.note: elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some upper-class aristocrats outdo even a skilled master.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is an expert performer, and a virtuoso is someone with outstanding skill, especially in music.

clue.text: Independent and Times misused English? Make a list

indicators.note: misused suggests the letters are put to the wrong order

explanation.surface: Two British newspapers mangle the language, so someone draws up a list of errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent and The Times are British newspapers; TIMES jumbled gives TEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set things out one by one, entry by entry.

clue.text: Inconsequential brief ménage à trois?

parts.note: trois is French for three, which is TRI as a prefix
a short-lived affair is a fling

explanation.surface: A short-lived threesome is dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: A ménage à trois is a three-person relationship; read literally, a brief one for three is a short affair with the Latin prefix for three in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling is trivial and unimportant, of no real consequence.

clue.text: National strike — big one — no end in sight anywhere

indicators.note: each word loses its last letter, so neither has an end

parts.note: to belt is to hit hard
a giant is a very large one

explanation.surface: A huge national strike drags on with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: BELT and GIANT each drop their final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian is a citizen of Belgium, someone of that nationality.

clue.text: Publicity issued by former recording company before debut performance

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
EMI was a British record label, now absorbed into others
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A former record label sends out press releases ahead of an opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public showing of a play or film.

clue.text: Mistakes made by informer found in time

indicators.note: found in means the informer sits inside the next word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: An informant's errors are uncovered in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed work, so the plural word means mistakes.

clue.text: Make charged particles in iron nails get neutralised intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on how iron nails become neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of 'iron nails get'; 'neutralised' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To ionise is to turn atoms into ions, atoms that carry an electric charge.

clue.text: Does moving up river in China

indicators.note: the letter rises to an earlier place in this down answer

parts.note: Sèvres is a famous French porcelain, a china
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A deer travels upstream on a river in China.
explanation.walkthrough: Does looks like female deer, but it is the verb. Sèvres porcelain comes from a town near Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve is to do or perform a duty, as in 'that will serve', so serves fits does.

clue.text: Fat girl on diet at last

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An overweight young woman finally goes on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is hard animal fat used in cooking, such as in puddings.

clue.text: Controlling German piece recalled Boris, for one

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol, a piece in gangster slang
Boris Johnson is a Tory, one of the UK Conservatives

explanation.surface: A German fragment of the past brings Boris to mind, as a control freak.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece is slang for a gun. Boris Johnson, former UK prime minister, is a Conservative, a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulatory bodies govern and supervise, so the adjective means governing or overseeing.

clue.text: Hat diacritic used in Spain, not Germany

indicators.note: not means the letter for Germany is left out

parts.note: the tilde is the wavy mark over the Spanish ñ
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A hat-shaped accent mark appears in Spanish but not German.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is old British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is dated slang for a hat, especially a silk top hat.

clue.text: Lay claim to property without right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the property goes round the letter

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property

explanation.surface: Someone claims land without any legal right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion, but here it means outside: ASSET goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly or insist on a right, which is staking a claim.

clue.text: Second American omitted from yearbook had charge cancelled

indicators.note: omitted means the named letter is left out

parts.note: an annual is a book published yearly
the second A in the word, A being the abbreviation for American
led means was in charge of

explanation.surface: A US student, left out of the yearbook, has a charge against them dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second A of ANNUAL goes, leaving ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Annulled means declared void or invalid, as a marriage or decision can be.
